key_insight: A staged LLM-to-FHIR pipeline can turn clinical case text into structured, interoperable EHR data for more realistic benchmarking of diagnostic reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This matters because models may perform differently on structured FHIR inputs than on plain text, so evaluation should match real clinical deployment formats.
method: Generate FHIR R4 bundles from unstructured case text using staged LLM prompting
Apply terminology-grounded validation and repair to reduce hallucinated codes and enforce consistency
Benchmark diagnostic reasoning on the resulting synthetic dataset aligned to clinician-authored cases
evidence_signal: The authors report valid FHIR generation for 82.5% of cases and find lower diagnostic accuracy on structured FHIR inputs than on plain text.
watch_item: Synthetic FHIR generation and validation may still miss real-world complexity, so results should be interpreted as benchmark evidence rather than direct clinical performance.
paper_title: MedCase-Structured: A Text-to-FHIR Dataset for Benchmarking Diagnostic Reasoning in Clinically Realistic EHR Settings
